title: Golden workbook fails its own values-mode verifier due to an unfixed oscillating circular reference, and values mode misses 5 of the 9 double-counting formula fixes
evidence: In spec.yaml, the sole verifier `SpreadsheetBench 2 official cell check` (`verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells`, weight: 1) grades in `mode: values` by recalculating `output_path` in LibreOffice (`managed_recalculated_xlsx(..., force_recalculation=True)`) and comparing the recalculated values against the un-recalculated Excel-cached values in `gt_10_golden.xlsx`. However, `gt_10_golden.xlsx` retains an oscillating circular reference in the debt/cash schedule (`Model!I195:M195` and `Model!I205:M205` reference Ending Cash `I$182:M$182` instead of Beginning Cash `I$180:M$180`, while `I182:M182 = SUM(I180:I181)` sums `I195:M195`, creating a non-convergent 2-cycle `I195_{t+1} = -2*I146 - I195_t` with slope -1). In `gt_10_golden.xlsx`, Excel stopped iterating at `iterateCount=100` mid-oscillation with internally inconsistent cached values: for example, `Model!J196` (`=SUM(J193:J195)`) has cached value `26.0387421711607`, whereas its cached inputs `J193=24.3085989919352`, `J194=2.73632181798672`, and `J195=-1.17853993270535` sum to `25.86638087721657`; similarly, `Model!I195` has cached value `-3.0727010080648`, whereas evaluating its formula on `gt_10_golden.xlsx`'s own cached inputs (`I146=1.96070379341113`, `I182=-0.111997214653663`, `K11=1`) yields `-0.848706578757467`. When `gt_10_golden.xlsx` itself is passed to `verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells`, LibreOffice recalculation lands on `Model!I195=-0.848706268009615`, `I182=2.04921163134373`, `I121=-3.08777611992694` (vs golden `-3.00406239978358`), causing `gt_10_golden.xlsx` to fail its own verifier with `score=0.0` (`regression 1.0000, modification 0.2911, 167 cell errors`: 16 regression errors and 151 modification errors across `Model` and `P&L Summary`). Additionally, in `mode: values`, 5 of the 9 formula fixes between input and golden (`Model!I45:M45`, changing `=SUM(I43,I41,I47)` to `=SUM(I43,I41)`) have identical cached values in the active Base Case (`$C$2=1`, where Revenue Synergies `I47:M47=0`) and are therefore never checked as modification cells.
confirmation: Confirmed: the Model!I195/I182/I181 circular loop and the iterate=true setting are present, and cached J196 does not equal the sum of its cached inputs J193:J195. A values-mode check against these stale caches fails the golden workbook itself.
fix: Same mode change. Formula mode grades all 9 fixes (Model I45:M45, I112, I164, P&L Summary G13, G32), including the 5 I45:M45 fixes whose values are identical in the Base Case, and no longer depends on the oscillating loop's values.

title: The golden workbook fails its own grading after mandatory recalculation
evidence: The sole verifier, weighted 1.0, force-recalculates submissions but compares them with the golden workbook's stored values. Passing gt_10_golden.xlsx through that same recalculation and cell-check pipeline produces regression 1.0000, modification 0.2911, and 167 mismatches, yielding an overall score of 0. For example, 'P&L Summary'!G40 is stored as 1.96070379341113 but recalculates to 1.89791789935335, outside the 1% tolerance. The retained iterative cash/debt calculations are not a stable reference: even the seed's 'Model'!I196 stores 24.5228320299134 although its formula SUM(I193:I195) sums to 25.275662480204897. Correct formula-based work can therefore fail against the supplied answer key.
confirmation: Same root cause: the golden workbook's stored values for the non-converging cash/debt loop are internally inconsistent (e.g. J196 vs SUM(J193:J195)), so the force-recalculated golden workbook does not match its own stored values.

title: The ground-truth file fails its own grading: after the LibreOffice recalc the verifier forces, the GT scores only 29% on the cells it changed
evidence: I copied gt_10_golden.xlsx in as the output and ran verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells with the spec's exact parameters. It forced a LibreOffice recalc and returned 'regression 1.0, modification 0.2911', with 167 cell errors. Examples: Model!I195 answer=-3.0727 vs output=-0.8487; Model!I181 answer=-1.1120 vs output=1.0492; Model!I182 answer=-0.1120 vs output=2.0492; Model!J186 answer=26.0387 vs output=29.2689; Model!I146 answer=1.9607 vs output=1.8979. The verifier is binary (weight 1). It passes only when every changed cell matches, so it cannot award 1.0 even to a perfect fix that is identical to the GT. The cause is a circular reference: the workbook uses iterative calculation (calcPr iterate="true" iterateCount="100" iterateDelta="0.0001"). The cash, revolver and interest loop is I182=SUM(I180:I181), I181=I146+I194+I195+I205, I195=...MIN(MAX(-I193-I194,-(I146+I194+(I182-$K$11))),0), and I121 interest uses I183=$H183*AVERAGE(I180,I182). I195 feeds back into itself with a coefficient of -1, so each iteration swings back and forth and never converges. The cached GT value (-3.07) and the LibreOffice value (-0.85) sit on either side of the fixed point (about -1.96, their average). Which value comes out depends on the engine and the iteration count, not on whether the fix is correct. Most of the 213 graded changed cells (Model rows 112-199 and I:N, plus downstream cells) sit in this loop.
confirmation: The I195 formula feeds I182 back with coefficient -1 under iterate=true/100. Cached I195 = -3.0727, while evaluating it on cached inputs gives a different value, so a LibreOffice recalc lands elsewhere and the GT fails its own check.
fix: Same mode change; the GT now passes its own check.

title: Golden gate: the ground-truth deliverable does not score full reward
evidence: The ground-truth deliverable, staged at the verifiers' own output paths and graded by the problem's real grader, scored 0.00 (need >= 1.00). A correct answer that does not earn full reward means a verifier false-negatives the mandated work. With the ground truth staged, every one of the 1 checks on /home/model/Desktop/output.xlsx scored 0 (summed weight 1.000), which is the whole shortfall of the GT grade. A correct deliverable does not fail every check at once; the ground truth for this file most likely never reached the grader (paired with a file of another type or name), so these are not 1 separate verifier defects.
